core.Health/max: A hundred hit points: a round number every damage figure is read against (CMB-01)
core.Resistance/hack: No armour: every unit is unarmoured until its template says otherwise
core.Resistance/pierce: No armour: every unit is unarmoured until its template says otherwise
core.Resistance/crush: No armour: every unit is unarmoured until its template says otherwise
core.Attack/Melee/hack: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/pierce: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/crush: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/reach: A block between the two bodies' edges, an arm's length
core.Attack/Melee/prepare: Half a second's wind-up before the first blow, so an attack reads
core.Vision/range: Twelve blocks: an enemy at the edge of the default camera's view is noticed (CMB-02)
core.Behaviour/flee: Units stand their ground unless their template says they run

strategos:template/unit_base.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: 3.75 blocks a second, a little under a walking player's 4.3, so a crowd reads as marching; M1's movement baselines are measured at it (D-11)
strategos:template/unit_base.UnitMotion/turnRate: Degrees a tick: a full turn in eight ticks, quick enough for orders to feel immediate, slow enough to see the turn
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/width: A player's hit box, so the vanilla humanoid model fits (D-04)
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/height: A player's hit box, so the vanilla humanoid model fits (D-04)
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/radius: The avoidance radius, a little over half the width, so a dense crowd still shows gaps between bodies (M1, PATH-06)

strategos:unit/debug_walker.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: Five blocks a second: the movement tests' brisk walker, never a game unit

strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/hack: With 100 hit points and resistance 5, one spearman kills another in 29 blows, about half a minute at a blow a second (M2, CMB-02)
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/reach: A spear reaches a little past an arm's length
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/prepare: Half a second's wind-up before the first thrust, so a charge reads
strategos:unit/infantry.Resistance/hack: 0.9^5 lets 59 % through: shield and padding make a fight between two spearmen last tens of seconds
strategos:unit/infantry.Resistance/crush: Padding does little against blunt blows; crush belongs to cavalry and siege later
strategos:unit/infantry.Cost/resources/wood: Forty wood: the shaft and the shield; wood gathered early goes to both houses and soldiers
strategos:unit/infantry.Cost/population: One house's room for one soldier, as for a worker
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/fire: Three fire a blow: ten spearmen burn a wooden house in 13.5 s and a stone civic centre in about two and a half minutes, so a raid hurts but alone does not end a match (CMB-03, D-12)
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/prepare: Half a second to light the torch and reach the wall, as the spear's wind-up
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/repeat: A blow of fire a second, the spear's rhythm

strategos:unit/worker.Health/max: Half a spearman's: a raid on workers costs their owner dearly, so workers are worth guarding
strategos:unit/worker.Behaviour/flee: Eight blocks from a blow: out of a spearman's reach, near enough to go back to work
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/resources/food: Sixty food: the civic centre's first worker pays back its cost in about a minute of berry picking
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/population: One house's room for one worker
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/time: Ten seconds: a civic centre with a full queue adds a worker every ten seconds, the pace the first house's timing target (1:30) assumes
strategos:unit/worker.Builder/rate: One builder's worth: a building's time is what one worker takes, and more builders add with diminishing returns (BLD-03)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/fruit: A berry a second: a bush's sixty food in a minute, so the first worker pays back its own cost quickly
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/grain: Half a berry picker's: a field's farmers are its steady food, five of them about two a second together (ECO-09)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/wood/tree: Slower than picking: a log's twenty wood in about half a minute, so an oak keeps a worker busy for a few minutes
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/stone/rock: Slower than chopping: a block's five stone in about twelve seconds, so a rock outcrop is a lasting job and stone stays dearer than wood (ECO-07)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/food: Ten food a trip: short trips, so a bush near the centre keeps food coming steadily
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/wood: Ten wood a trip, half a log: eight trips pay for the first house (the timing target, 1:30)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/stone: Ten stone a trip, two blocks: twenty trips pay a civic centre's two hundred
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/iron/ore: A little slower than stone: a mine's iron is the scarcest resource, so iron sets the pace of an army (ECO-08)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/iron: Ten iron a trip, as stone
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/meat: As fruit's: a carcass is the quickest food once killed, which pays for the walk to the herd
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/slaughter: Hit points a blow, one a second: a sheep in four, a chicken in two

resource_yield.#minecraft:logs: Twenty wood a log: an oak of four or five logs holds about ninety, a few minutes of one worker's chopping
resource_yield.#minecraft:leaves: Leaves yield nothing: they are the canopy that thins as a tree is felled (ECO-03)
resource_yield.#minecraft:base_stone_overworld: Five stone a block of rock: indexed now, gathered from ECO-07 (M4)
resource_yield.#c:ores/iron: Ten iron a block of ore: indexed now, gathered from ECO-08 (M4)
resource_yield.minecraft:wheat: A field's crop: its food is the field's own amount, not the block's (ECO-09)
resource_yield.minecraft:sweet_berry_bush: Sixty food a bush, a worker's cost; a bush left alone fills again in ten minutes, but an emptied one stays empty: early food that runs out, so fields matter (ECO-09)

strategos:building/civic_centre.Health/max: Two thousand: ten spearmen with torches take minutes, so a raid alone does not end a match (CMB-03)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/wood: Three hundred wood: a second centre is a late, deliberate expansion, not an opening move
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/stone: Two hundred stone: stone matters from M4; until then only the starting centre exists
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/time: Two and a half minutes: the largest build of the first loop
strategos:building/civic_centre.Housing/capacity: Twenty: the five starting workers and fifteen more before the first house is needed
strategos:building/civic_centre.Placement/civicReach: None: a civic centre stands where its spacing allows, not near another
strategos:building/civic_centre.Placement/spacing: Sixty-four blocks between centres: a second centre claims new ground, not a corner of the first's
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/iron: A hundred iron: a second centre's tools and fittings, a late investment (ECO-08)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Limit/count: One civic centre a faction until phases (Town) allow more, as in the classics (BLD-08)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Trainer/batchExponent: Five in 5^0.8 ≈ 3.6 units' time: a batch saves 28 %, worth tying the money up for (PROD-02, as the classics)

strategos:template/building_base.Placement/civicReach: Within 48 blocks of an own centre's footprint: a town grows round its centre, the stand-in for territory until TERR-02
strategos:template/building_base.Resistance/fire: Stone: 0.9^7 lets 48 % of a torch's fire through, so wood burns more than twice as fast per hit point (CMB-03)
strategos:template/building_base.Health/max: Five hundred: what a structure without its own figure holds; a deposit has it too, though nothing in M4 attacks one
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/first: The first blocks fall once a seventh of the building is gone, early enough to show an attack is working (BLD-05, 04 §11.8)
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/second: Two thirds of its hit points left: a third of its blocks down, the building plainly hurt
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/third: A third left: most of it down but its walls' foot, a ruin still standing until its last hit points

strategos:building/house.Health/max: Four hundred: a house burns in well under a minute to a squad (CMB-03)
strategos:building/house.Cost/resources/wood: Eighty wood: a worker's first trip or two to a tree; the first house by 1:30 (the timing target)
strategos:building/house.Housing/capacity: Five: a house a few trainings, so housing paces growth
strategos:building/house.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)

strategos:building/field.Health/max: Two hundred: a field burns quickly, a cheap thing to raid
strategos:building/field.Cost/resources/wood: Sixty wood: a worker's first two trips to a tree, after the berries run low
strategos:building/field.Cost/time: Twenty seconds: a field goes in faster than a house
strategos:building/field.Footprint/obstructs: No: farmers stand on their field, and units walk through the crop
strategos:building/field.Field/amount: Three hundred food a sowing: five farmers reap it in about two and a half minutes
strategos:building/field.Field/ripenTime: Thirty seconds to ripen, while its farmers wait
strategos:building/field.Field/reseed/wood: Forty wood to sow again: cheaper than a new field, so a reseed is the habit (D-14)
strategos:building/field.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)

strategos:building/barracks.Health/max: Twelve hundred: between a house and the centre
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/wood: Two hundred wood: the barracks by 4:00 (the timing target) after a house and steady chopping
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/stone: A hundred stone: soldiers need the quarry, so stone matters from the first barracks; the first loop's starts bring a hundred (ECO-07, BLD-08)
strategos:building/barracks.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/iron: Fifty iron: the spear points and helmets of the barracks' armoury; the first loop's starts bring a hundred (ECO-08)
strategos:building/barracks.Trainer/batchExponent: As the civic centre's: one rule for every trainer until a technology changes it (TECH-05)

strategos:building/quarry.Deposit/amount: A thousand stone, two hundred quarried blocks' worth: a small quarry pays a civic centre five times over and lasts a match's opening (ECO-08)
strategos:building/quarry.Deposit/slots: Three workers at a small quarry: a third of a field's, so stone comes slower than food

strategos:building/quarry_large.Deposit/amount: Five thousand stone: the contested deposit a town grows towards (ECO-08)
strategos:building/quarry_large.Deposit/slots: Six workers at a large quarry, twice a small one's

strategos:building/iron_mine.Deposit/amount: A thousand iron: a small mine pays for twenty spearmen's iron and a centre's (ECO-08)
strategos:building/iron_mine.Deposit/slots: Three workers at a small mine, as at a small quarry

strategos:building/iron_mine_large.Deposit/amount: Five thousand iron: the contested mine of the middle game (ECO-08)
strategos:building/iron_mine_large.Deposit/slots: Six workers at a large mine, twice a small one's

strategos:template/unit_fauna.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: Two blocks a second, an animal's amble; they stand where they are put until they wander (spec §1.6 row 11)

strategos:unit/sheep.Health/max: Four of a worker's blows, so a slaughter takes four seconds, about a farm trip's walk
strategos:unit/sheep.Fauna/meat: The classic opening sheep: ten worker trips of food, a hundred, as much as a berry bush holds
strategos:unit/sheep.Fauna/slots: Three workers round one animal, as round a bush: more crowd it
strategos:unit/sheep.Body/width: Vanilla's sheep, 0.9 blocks wide, so its model fits
strategos:unit/sheep.Body/radius: Half its width: it keeps others off its body

strategos:unit/pig.Health/max: Five blows: the bigger animal takes a moment longer
strategos:unit/pig.Fauna/meat: Half again a sheep's, as a heavier animal

strategos:unit/chicken.Fauna/meat: Four worker trips: a snack that starts the first minutes
strategos:unit/chicken.Body/radius: Its half width rounded up, so its body stays clear

strategos:building/storehouse.Health/max: Between a house and a barracks: a stone store, worth raiding
strategos:building/storehouse.Cost/resources/wood: A house's and a fifth: the first building a growing economy adds by its woods and rocks
strategos:building/storehouse.Cost/resources/stone: Half a barracks' stone: stone's third buyer, so a quarry pays for itself early
strategos:building/storehouse.Cost/time: Forty seconds, 3.2 blocks a second for its 128 (the style guide's 1.5–6)

strategos:building/farmstead.Health/max: A house's and a half: a farm building of mud and brick
strategos:building/farmstead.Cost/resources/wood: As a storehouse: the food side's dropsite costs what the other side's does, less its stone
strategos:building/farmstead.Cost/time: Thirty-five seconds, 2.5 blocks a second for its 88
strategos:building/farmstead.Reseeder/reach: Twenty-four blocks: a ring of fields round the farmstead, as the classics' farm by the mill (ECO-17, D-14)

strategos:gather_wood_1.cost/food: 100 food: what the classic first wood-gathering tech costs, 100 food and 50 wood (docs/research/mechanics.md §1.3, the Double-Bit Axe row)
strategos:gather_wood_1.cost/wood: 50 wood: the same row of the table, 100 food and 50 wood, so the tech is paid from both sides of the economy (docs/research/mechanics.md §1.3)
strategos:gather_wood_1.time: Thirty seconds, three workers' training: the classics' first wood tech takes about forty (docs/research/mechanics.md, economy techs); our own starting value, tuned against QA-12 in M6 T23
strategos:gather_wood_1.effects/0/value: A fifth faster felling: the classics' first wood tech gives a quarter (docs/research/mechanics.md, economy techs); ours is a smaller first step, our own starting value, tuned against QA-12 in M6 T23
